paragraphs: Rabbi Zakkai, in chapter Hamotzi Yayin 79b, in Rabbi Shimon’s name. A tanna of the baraita, described [by Sefer Yuchasin] as a student of Rabbi Shimon Berabbi. I do not know where he derives that he was Shimon Berabbi’s student (see what I wrote at length in the rules). I do not understand it thus, for unqualified Rabbi Shimon is known to be Shimon ben Yochai (see his entry). Further compelling proof: it says there, “Rabbi Shimon ben Yehudah says in Rabbi Shimon’s name …; Rabbi Zakkai says in his name,” meaning Rabbi Shimon; so too Rabbi Shimshon on Yadayim 3:3. Shimon ben Yehudah was Rabbi’s colleague (see his entry), mentioned often in the Mishnah (see his entry). He necessarily reports Shimon ben Yochai, Rabbi’s teacher; many times Shimon ben Yehudah reports Rabbi Shimon (see his entry). Shimon Berabbi is never mentioned in the Mishnah, except Makkot 3:15. How could Zakkai’s colleague be Shimon ben Yehudah, mentioned in the Mishnah, while his colleague Zakkai was Shimon Berabbi’s student? Moreover, Shimon ben Yehudah and Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon disagree; Elazar was Shimon ben Yochai’s son. How could Zakkai, Shimon ben Yehudah’s colleague, be Shimon Berabbi’s student? In Berakhot 25b, Zakkai disputes Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel and Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar. See Shimon ben Elazar, Rabbi’s colleague; Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel was Rabbi’s father. How could Zakkai be Shimon Berabbi’s student? Truth thus shows its path: he testified falsely. In Niddah 41b:“Come and hear, for Rabbi Zakkai recites.”
